subject: Urgent: Edge traffic reshuffle — immediate reroute instructions and post-incident checklist
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Horizon Retail Ops <ops@horizonretail.com>, Emily Park <emily.park@horizonretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2029-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: Edge traffic reshuffle — immediate reroute instructions and post-incident checklist

Hi Emily / Horizon Ops team,

We observed a targeted control-plane disruption affecting a subset of our EU edge fabric (regions: eu-west-1, eu-central-1) and intermittent packet loss in APAC peering that is causing elevated 5xx rates for a small percentage of API calls from those regions. Our mitigation is to temporarily steer traffic away from affected edge POPs while we validate and repair the underlying peering and control-plane subsystems.

What we need from you now (recommended, low-effort options):
- Short-term: point your region header or regional endpoint preference to our US fallback cluster to avoid the impacted POPs. Two options:
  1) Swap region header: set X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2 on requests (no code change in most HTTP clients).
  2) Use the dedicated failover endpoint: https://us-failover.api.redwoodinference.com (DNS TTL updated; supports same API keys).
- If you use embedded routing in sidecars or client SDK, set region_preference=["us-west-2","us-east-1"] for the next 48 hours.
- If you have a hard affinity pinned to EU/APAC for compliance reasons, reply to confirm and we will provide a scoped SLA exception and a narrow routing config that minimizes cross-region exposure.

Attachments: reroute-runbook.pdf (PDF, 320KB) — step-by-step call examples, SDK snippets, and rollback steps.

We will keep this thread for customer-facing coordination. Internal notes and ongoing operator logs are in INF-2145 (JIRA). Expect a short confirmation request from our SREs for a scheduled switch, and please reply to confirm whether you want us to proceed with an automated failover on your behalf.

Apologies for the disruption — our priority is to keep your production traffic healthy while we fully remediate.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
T: +1-415-555-0187
Attachment: reroute-runbook.pdf (PDF, 320KB)

From: Horizon Retail Ops <ops@horizonretail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Park <emily.park@horizonretail.com>
Date: 2029-07-19T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Edge traffic reshuffle — immediate reroute instructions and post-incident checklist

Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick note and the runbook. We see elevated errors in our EU storefront write traffic and need to confirm a few things before moving traffic:
1) Will the US fallback endpoint preserve request ordering/consistency for our high-volume cart writes (we rely on idempotency tokens)?
2) Any change to token validation / session affinity we should be aware of?

If those look fine, pls proceed with automated failover and copy our SRE (oliver@zephyr.ai) — he will help monitor. We prefer Redwood to manage the switch to avoid rush changes on our side.

— Alex (on behalf of Horizon Retail Ops)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2029-07-19T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Urgent: Edge traffic reshuffle — internal runbook and SRE checklist

Vanessa / Dylan —

Internal ops plan being kicked off. TL;DR: we can do automated failover for Horizon Retail using the failover endpoint; it preserves idempotency and token validation since the routing happens at the edge layer and the auth service is global. Actions we have taken/are taking:
- INF-2145 created and assigned to SRE pod 4 (lead: K. Huang).
- Prepared the following artifacts: reroute-runbook.pdf, quick-rollback.sh (scripts included in the runbook), and edge-connect-trace.log (sample traces).
- Rolling failover plan: staged DNS update and edge route weight change (50% -> 100% over 3 mins) with automated rollback on >1% error increase.

Planned comm cadence:
- 10:15am: notify Horizon we're about to start (we have their permission).
- 10:20am: start staged switch to us-failover cluster (see runbook).
- 10:30am: verify 2xx% and token validation metrics; if stable, complete.
- 12:00pm: post-incident status update to customers and link to postmortem.

Attachments: edge-connect-trace.log (text, 120KB) — pasted a short sample below.

Marissa
Senior Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

--

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Horizon Retail Ops <ops@horizonretail.com>, Emily Park <emily.park@horizonretail.com>, Oliver James <sre@zephyr.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2029-07-20T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: edge reshuffle complete and follow-ups (Horizon Retail)

Hi Alex / Emily / Oliver,

Summary (short): we completed the planned reroute to the US fallback cluster for Horizon Retail at 10:22am PST on 2029-07-19. The staged switch succeeded; your API error rate dropped to baseline within the 3-minute ramp window and we observed no data loss or ordering regressions. Full timeline and evidence are linked below.

What happened:
- Root cause: transient BGP flap affecting two EU POP transit providers combined with a control-plane heartbeat regression in the EU control fabric.
- Impact: elevated 5xx rates and connection resets for ~6% of EU-originating requests; unrelated APAC peering jitter caused a smaller set of customer sessions to experience retries.

Remediation performed:
- Immediate: automated reroute to us-failover.api.redwoodinference.com for affected customers who consented (Horizon Retail opted in).
- Ongoing: patch applied to control-plane heartbeat backoff and transit provider engaged for peering fixes.

Customer-facing artifacts attached/linked:
- Postmortem draft: https://dashboard.redwoodinference.com/postmortem/incident-2029-07-19
- Runbook we executed: reroute-runbook.pdf
- Operator traces: edge-connect-trace.log

Next steps for Horizon Retail (recommended):
1) Verify your ingestion/analytics pipelines for any retry duplicates (we did not observe duplicates, but confirm).
2) If you want a permanent cross-region affinity change, submit a support ticket referencing INF-2145 and we will schedule a design call.
3) We will follow up within 48 hours with a finalized postmortem and a proposed SLA credit if you experienced >=5 minutes of degraded availability.

If you have any further questions or need us to keep the failover in place longer, tell us the window and we’ll accommodate.

Thanks again for the collaboration; Oliver, appreciate you standing by.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0187
